subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should device-less network shared-token WebSocket operator clients receive operator scopes through a server-derived policy such as gateway.auth.tokenScopes, or should OpenClaw keep requiring device identity/pairing for write/admin scopes?
rationale: The observable bug is real at source level, but the repair changes which remote clients can exercise operator.write or stronger scopes after possessing a shared token, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent trust boundary.

options.title: Continue Bounded Token Scopes
options.body: Review and land a server-configured token-scope contract with non-loopback and privileged-scope guards, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Require Device Identity
options.body: Keep device-less shared-token clients scope-empty and direct affected deployments to device tokens or pairing rather than granting write scopes by token alone.

options.title: Reject The Behavior Change
options.body: Close this issue as current security policy if maintainers decide remote shared-token clients must never gain operator scopes without device identity.

recommendation.title: Continue Bounded Token Scopes
recommendation.body: Review and land a server-configured token-scope contract with non-loopback and privileged-scope guards, docs, tests, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the current tokenScopes proposal and has recent commits in the affected Gateway auth/config surface.
